column1: # Generated by `make frequencies` — do not edit by hand.

# FineFreq (Binbin Xu, arXiv:2512.09701, CC BY 4.0): https://github.com/Bin-2/FineFreq — pinned commit 79a6bd84a7a188ebf95d66fb4b20e344d4937e3a; per-language character frequency tables from FineWeb/FineWeb2 (Common Crawl, 2013-2025).

# Leipzig Corpora Collection (D. Goldhahn, T. Eckart & U. Quasthoff, LREC 2012), CC BY 4.0: https://wortschatz.uni-leipzig.de — non-normalized per-language sentence corpora, used to estimate the characters FineFreq's own NFKC normalization discards; corpus ids per language are pinned in this script.

# Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 29th edition (2026), SIL Global, as reproduced in Wikipedia's "List of languages by total number of speakers" (revision 1342539322) — total speakers (L1+L2) for the top 40 languages by that count.

# Method: each FineFreq table is normalized to a probability distribution over non-whitespace, non-control, non-format, non-private-use, non-surrogate, non-unassigned code points; characters NFKC folds out of FineFreq are estimated from a Leipzig corpus calibrated onto FineFreq's scale, then un-folded back out of their NFKC expansion; per-code distributions are mixed by Ethnologue speaker count times FineFreq script share and truncated to a share >= 1.00e-05.
